the cross talk between TLR2 and PPARγ signaling pathway in peritoneal macrophaes and the possible mechanisms involved in this interaction.
the cross-talk between PPARγ, TLR2, ERK and JUN MAP kinases in mouse peritoneum macrophages.
the role of MAPK signaling pathways and PPARγ in macrophage activation by peptidoglican.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PGN induces biphasic effect in PPARγ expression and the MAP kinase signaling is involved in PPARγ regulation.
the PGN induced early activation of ERK and later activation of JNK MAP kinseases leads to biphasical expression of PPARγ in mouse peritonea macrophages.
PGN induced early upregulation of PPARγ is mediated by ERK MAPK, which in turn attenuates NF-κB activation, while the late inhibition is mediated by JNK MAPK, which may enhance NF-κB signaling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
peptidoylglycan (PG) induces PPARγ which attenuates NF-κB activation via MAPKs activation.
PPARγ expression is regulated by MAP kinases and PPARγ in return attenuates the NF-κB signaling pathway.
the activation of PPARγ by peptidogylcan (PGN), which is a TLR2 ligand, attenuates NF-κB pathway and thus inhibits inflammatory cytokines production in mouse peritonea macrophages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PGN treatment induces PPARγ which in turn suppresses inflammatory responses by inhibiting NF-κB activation.
PGN induced PPARγ expression is regulated by MAP kinases and this enhanced PPRγ attenuates NF-κB activation in a p65-dependent manner.
PPARγ is a key player in macrophage response to PGN and it may have therapeutic implications for inflammatory diseases.
